thread.title: Global Equity Funds Suffer Worst Money Outflow In At Least 14 Years

author: APARNA NARAYANAN
title: Global Equity Funds Suffer Worst Money Outflow In At Least 14 Years
text:
Investors stampeded out of equities this week as market volatility spiked across the world, triggering the worst weekly net outflow of money in more than a decade. But there was one area that saw an increase.
X They pulled a net $30.6 billion out of global equity funds in the week through Wednesday, according to EPFR Global, marking the biggest loss since at least 2004.
The U.S. was especially hard hit. U.S. stock funds leaked $34 billion in the five trading days through Wednesday. Funds investing in stocks from developed European countries saw $3.4 billion in withdrawals, while Asia Pacific funds shed $7.7 billion, the Financial Times said.
However, emerging markets bucked the trend, pulling in $2.1 billion.
For the week, the Dow Jones industrial average lost 5.2%. Boeing ( BA ), which helped power much of the Dow's earlier gains, lost 4.5%. Among other big Dow names, Apple ( AAPL ) fell 2.7%, and Caterpillar ( CAT ) dropped 5.3%.
The S&P 500 dropped 5.2% this week and the Nasdaq lost 5.1%, as tech leaders like Amazon ( AMZN ), Facebook ( FB ) and Netflix ( NFLX ) have given up 6.3%, 7.5% and 6.7%, respectively.
